chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from 'Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: May a man speak during the adhan? He said: There is no harm. I said: During the iqamah? He said: No.

key_terms.الْأَذَانِ: the call announcing the time of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: the call immediately preceding the commencement of salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَا: no; a negation indicating prohibition here
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during the adhan or iqamah?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between speaking during the adhan and speaking during the iqamah. It indicates that speaking during the adhan is permitted, while speaking during the iqamah is not permitted, reflecting the greater immediacy and sanctity of the iqamah before salat.
